label: misaligned
reason: The formal conclusion provides an ambient extension only on J = [a,b] intersect (t0-epsilon,t0+epsilon), with no requirement that J cover [a,b]. Although Phi is typed as a real-indexed family of diffeomorphisms, both joint smoothness and Phi_t(gamma_t0(z)) = gamma_t(z) are asserted only on J. The bound target requires an ambient isotopy extending the entire given isotopy; its scope permits a circle source and a finite-dimensional real ambient space, but no restriction to a local time window. A further gluing or continuation theorem is needed to obtain that conclusion. The local extension lemma can be valid while failing to state the full target.

witness_coverage_example.setup: Take E = R^2, a=0, b=1, alpha=-1, beta=2, t0=0, and gamma_t(z)=c(z)+t*e1 for the standard smoothly embedded circle c.
witness_coverage_example.witness: Choose epsilon=1/10. Define Phi_t(x)=x+t*e1 when abs(t)<1/10 and Phi_t(x)=x otherwise. Each Phi_t is a diffeomorphism, Phi_0 is the identity, and the evaluation map is jointly smooth on E times J=[0,1/10). The required extension equation holds on J.
witness_coverage_example.missing_property: At t=1, Phi_1 is the identity, so Phi_1(gamma_0(z)) is not gamma_1(z). The family is also not smooth in time at the edge of the local window, which the formal conclusion does not constrain.
witness_coverage_example.limitation: The translating circle does admit a full ambient isotopy. This example only shows that a witness satisfying the selected local conclusion need not satisfy the full target; it does not refute the local existence lemma.
